title: Iteration Patterns and Trace Tables
learningObjectives: Recognize common iteration patterns: count, accumulate, search and filter.
Trace loop state with a table.
Choose termination and early-exit logic appropriately.
Test empty, boundary and typical data.
Review loop clarity, correctness and complexity.

understand.concept: Common iteration patterns include counting, accumulation, searching, filtering and nested traversal. Trace tables record state, condition, action and update for each pass.
understand.whyItMatters: Pattern recognition helps choose a loop and test it systematically.
understand.explain: Test empty, boundary and typical cases; trace state changes and verify termination.

examples.title: Search early exit
examples.explanation: Search stops at first match and records success.

examples.title: Trace while loop
examples.explanation: State trace: 1→2→4→8; stops after x becomes 8.

practise.guidedTask: For Iteration Patterns and Trace Tables, trace each example in a table showing the loop's initial state, condition result, body action, update step, and final state. Identify the termination point and boundary behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ exercise focused on Iteration Patterns and Trace Tables. Include at least three test cases (typical, boundary and termination/invalid-input case where relevant), trace the loop iterations, and explain why it stops or skips/continues as intended.
hints: Write down the loop's starting state.
Trace the condition before/after each pass according to loop type.
Check that every continuing path progresses toward termination.
Test boundary values and early-exit paths.
Count passes explicitly to catch off-by-one errors.
